root_cause.text: An incorrect bounds check in the AMD IOMMU debugfs MMIO offset handler (`iommu_mmio_write`) validated offsets as if accesses were 4 bytes, while `iommu_mmio_show` actually performs an 8-byte `readq()` on that offset, allowing reads past `mmio_phys_end`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (iommu->dbg_mmio_offset > iommu->mmio_phys_end - 4)` to `if (iommu->dbg_mmio_offset > iommu->mmio_phys_end - sizeof(u64))`, and the CVE/commit text explicitly states that `iommu_mmio_show()` uses `readq()` and that an offset of `mmio_phys_end - 4` passes the old check but causes a 4-byte out-of-bounds read.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the MMIO write bounds check to use the full u64 access size and reject out-of-range end-of-region writes.
intent_record.what: The boundary check in iommu_mmio_write() was changed from comparing iommu->dbg_mmio_offset against iommu->mmio_phys_end - 4 to comparing it against iommu->mmio_phys_end - sizeof(u64).
intent_record.how: This adjusts the valid MMIO write range to account for an 8-byte access size instead of a hardcoded 4-byte limit, preventing writes near the end of the MMIO region from being incorrectly accepted when a full u64 write would extend past the mapped boundary.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the MMIO write bounds check to use the full u64 access size and reject out-of-range end-of-region writes.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the root cause: the MMIO offset bounds check was validating as if accesses were smaller than the actual 8-byte readq(), and this change updates the check to account for full u64 access size and block end-of-region out-of-bounds accesses.

candidates.rationale: This is the faulty bounds check: it only reserves 4 bytes at the end of the MMIO region, but the corresponding read path performs an 8-byte readq() from this offset. That mismatch permits offsets that cause the 8-byte access to extend past mmio_phys_end.

vuln_statements.explanation: This bounds check is the root cause of the vulnerability. It validates the debugfs MMIO offset as though only 4 bytes will be accessed, but the show path performs an 8-byte readq() at that offset. As a result, offsets within the last 4 bytes of the region are incorrectly accepted, allowing the subsequent 8-byte MMIO read to extend past mmio_phys_end.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it includes both the write-side bounds check and the read-side MMIO access. The vulnerable construct is present in `iommu_mmio_write()`: `if (iommu->dbg_mmio_offset > iommu->mmio_phys_end - 4)` validates the offset as if only 4 bytes are accessed. But `iommu_mmio_show()` performs `value = readq(iommu->mmio_base + iommu->dbg_mmio_offset);`, which is an 8-byte read. Therefore an offset in the range `(mmio_phys_end - 7)` through `(mmio_phys_end - 4)` would pass the check yet allow `readq()` to access past `mmio_phys_end`. Since the code uses `- 4` instead of enforcing space for an 8-byte read, the bug is present, and the fix is not yet included.
